findings.title: safe_urlopen() not wrapped in try/except
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch(), `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is called OUTSIDE the try/except block. Network errors, DNS failures, connection timeouts, or GitHub returning 5xx will raise an exception and produce a generic 500 error page instead of the user-friendly error page rendered by the `error()` helper. The try/except block below only covers `safe_urlread`, `decode`, and `parse_qsl` failures. The same applies to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 — any exception there will also bubble up as a 500. Both calls should be wrapped so transient failures degrade gracefully.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters not URL-encoded
findings.body: The OAuth authorize URL is built via f-string interpolation: `f"{...}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`. Neither `state` (currently `pipeline.signature`, an md5 hex digest, so safe today) nor `redirect_uri` is URL-encoded. If `redirect_uri` ever contains reserved characters (`&`, `?`, `=`, `#`, etc.), or if `pipeline.signature` generation changes, GitHub will parse the query string incorrectly and the OAuth callback state verification will fail or — worse — allow query parameters to bleed into `state`/`redirect_uri`. Use `urllib.parse.urlencode` for the query string.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found doesn't exercise the 404 path
findings.body: The test is named `test_installation_not_found` and stubs `/app/installations/{installation_id}` to return 404, but the assertion only checks for the generic "Invalid installation request." string. Tracing the flow: the first request to `setup_path` with `installation_id` triggers OAuthLoginView, which redirects to GitHub (no call to the 404 endpoint). The second request carries a hardcoded `state` of `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` that does NOT match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView short-circuits on the state check and returns `error()` before `build_integration` is ever reached. The 404 stub is never hit. The test silently passes for the wrong reason. To actually test the 404 path, the state must match the pipeline signature (e.g., capture it from the redirect on the first request, like other tests do indirectly via `assert_setup_flow`).

findings.title: Hardcoded HMAC signature will mismatch the modified body
findings.body: In `test_github_user_mismatch` the webhook is posted with the hardcoded header `HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE="sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486"`, but the request body is `json.dumps(webhook_event)` after the test mutates `installation.id` and `sender.login`. That HMAC was presumably computed over the unmodified `INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE` bytes. Standard GitHub webhook handlers verify the signature against the raw request body and reject mismatches (typically with a 401/403). When the handler rejects the webhook, no `Integration` record with `sender.login == "attacker"` is created, and the subsequent user-mismatch check in `GitHubInstallation` won't fire as intended. Either compute the signature dynamically from the mutated payload using the test webhook secret, or fix the signature for the actual bytes posted. This test should currently be failing or is silently broken.

findings.title: No tests for the new OAuth error branches
findings.body: OAuthLoginView introduces four new error branches that all funnel into the same `error()` helper and are therefore indistinguishable to callers: (1) `state` parameter mismatch, (2) GitHub returning no `access_token` in the token-exchange response, (3) `get_user_info` returning no `login`, and (4) the GitHubInstallation-level user mismatch (which is tested but only via the generic template assertion). Each of these is a distinct failure mode documented in the PR description ("state mismatch", "wrong or re-used code", "authenticate user mismatch") and should have a dedicated test that verifies the request reaches the expected code path and that the failure is rendered. The current `test_github_user_mismatch` only asserts `b"Invalid installation request."` and doesn't distinguish user mismatch from a state or token failure.

findings.title: OAuth scope not requested, but no scope validation either
findings.body: OAuthLoginView does not include a `scope` parameter when redirecting to GitHub's authorize URL. The access token returned will have only the default user:email scope (or whatever GitHub grants by default). `get_user_info` only uses `/user`, which works under the default scope, but if Sentry ever tries to use the resulting token for anything requiring an additional scope (e.g., reading private email, listing org installations), the request will silently 404/403. This is informational; consider either requesting the scopes Sentry actually needs explicitly (`scope=user:email read:org`), or documenting that only the default user-scope token is intended.

findings.title: KeyError possible if Integration has no 'sender' in metadata
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch the user-mismatch check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. Existing Integration rows created before this PR shipped (or rows created via paths that don't populate `sender`, e.g., legacy migrations) will have no `sender` key in `metadata`, raising `KeyError` and surfacing a 500 instead of the intended error page. The check should be guarded — e.g., treat a missing `sender` as a failed validation (`return error(...)`) or use `.get()` with a default. Otherwise the new security check will break upgrades.
